claims.content: To complete a transaction for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: To complete a transaction for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: A Customer with won auction items initiates checkout, chooses which items to pay for, selects a shipping method, selects a payment type, and thereby completes the transaction.
scope_contract.start_boundary: Customer has won auction items and begins the checkout/payment process.
scope_contract.success_boundary: Customer has selected the items to pay for, chosen a shipping method, and selected a payment type to complete the transaction.
in_scope_actions: Selecting which won auction items to pay for
excluded_adjacent_actions: Auction award or post-auction administrative processing
Downstream order processing outside this checkout
variant_dimensions: Which won items are selected for payment

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has at least one won auction item that remains unpaid (unpaid auction winnings).
The Customer has previously chosen either PayPal or Amazon Payments as their default Method of Payment (MOP).
The Customer's account is not in a 'Review' status.

The Customer triggers the use case by clicking the 'Winnings Alert' link, by clicking the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, or by clicking the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button.
The Customer selects which won auction items to pay for from the list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods.
The Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The system gets the Customer started on the payment process for their winnings.
The Customer selects a checkout option/payment type by clicking one of the available buttons ('Check out with PayPal', 'Check out with Amazon', or 'Checkout Later').

Diverges from Step 2: if the Customer is a returning user with a default Method of Payment of PayPal or Amazon Payments, the system routes them to a specific page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process for their winnings.
Diverges from Step 5: the Customer may select PayPal as their payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 5: the Customer may select 'Credit Card' as a new payment method in the 'My New Payment Method' section and enter new billing address details (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country) to complete the transaction.

Diverges from Step 5: if the Customer already has a PayPal account, they may log in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page, rather than creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 5: the Customer may choose to create a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account' and entering Country (defaulted to United States), then choosing either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card' as the payment method.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer selects the 'Checkout Later' button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a warning that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the window expires. The checkout is not completed at this time.

Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer does not complete payment for won items within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, the orders are cancelled and the items are placed into a 'Hold' status.

Diverges from Step 5: If a PayPal/Amazon Payments default customer's unpaid orders expire (unresolved/unpaid auction winnings older than 7 days), the system automatically locks the account and places it into 'Review Status'; the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying because the orders have already been cancelled.
Diverges from Step 5: If the Customer fails to complete the payment transaction within seven days (168 hours) of the auction's closing date/time, the Customer's account may be suspended.

missing_aspects: Payment provider authorization or decline handling during payment type selection

claims.content: Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and provides a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
For each won auction item for which the transaction has been successfully completed, the 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid'.
